2: name: reference-ui-fidelity
3: description: ALWAYS invoke before implementing or materially changing a product UI when a specification, mood board, HTML prototype, screenshot, Figma/OpenDesign artifact, or reference application exists. Converts the reference into a complete screen/state inventory, treats it as a visual acceptance oracle, and requires screenshot evidence before completion. Triggers on reference app, reference UI, standalone HTML, prototype, mood board, screenshot, attached image, match this design, visual fidelity, pixel parity, redesign, product shell, all screens, design spec.
4: ---
5: <!-- TJ-ARCH-MOB-001 compliant -->
6: 
7: > **Binding:** Treat the supplied reference as the acceptance oracle while
8: > preserving strict layering and accessibility. Project-local rules supplement,
9: > but do not replace, the self-contained verification contract below.
10: 
11: # Reference UI Fidelity Gate
12: 
13: A reference design is an acceptance oracle, not loose inspiration. Do not start from a
14: generic scaffold and hope to style it later. First extract the product system, full screen
15: inventory, component grammar, responsive behavior, and meaningful states from the
16: reference; then implement and compare the running app against it.
17: 
18: ## 1. Discover the authority set
19: 
20: Before editing UI, locate and inspect all applicable sources:
21: 
22: 1. product/functional specification;
23: 2. UI/UX standard and brand guide;
24: 3. mood board and user journeys;
25: 4. executable HTML/Figma/OpenDesign prototype;
26: 5. supplied screenshots in every theme and form factor; and
27: 6. current implementation and existing visual-regression evidence.
28: 
29: Record precedence when they conflict. A direct, newer user instruction wins over an older
30: mockup mechanic. Preserve the reference's product intent while applying the newer rule.
31: 
32: Locate this project's actual artifacts before starting — do not assume a given file
33: exists. If a project has none of them, say so and stop: there is no acceptance oracle
34: to build against, and inventing one produces confident, unreviewable output.
35: 
36: ## 2. Build a coverage matrix before code
37: 
38: Create an explicit matrix with one row per destination and meaningful state. At minimum:
39: 
40: | Dimension | Required inventory |
41: |---|---|
42: | Destinations | Every route/navigation destination visible in the reference |
43: | Themes | Light and dark |
44: | Form factors | Phone, tablet/medium, desktop/wide |
45: | Data states | Empty, populated, loading/streaming, degraded, error |
46: | Interaction states | Hover, focus, active, selected, disabled, expanded |
47: | Runtime states | Ready, model download/load, offline, local, owned remote, cloud |
48: 
49: It is a blocking failure to implement only the easiest routes while presenting the shell as
50: the reference application. Navigation items may not lead to placeholders or nowhere.
51: 
52: ## 3. Extract the visual grammar
53: 
54: Convert the reference into reusable, semantic decisions:
55: 
56: - surface ladder and theme tokens;
57: - typography roles and density;
58: - spacing/radius/motion scales;
59: - responsive shell and navigation transitions;
60: - component families and repeated compositions;
61: - status/provenance language; and
62: - content hierarchy and empty/error behavior.
63: 
64: Use `hybrid-design-tokens` for the shared token source. Use Shadcn UI for React primitives,
65: Assistant UI for chat/thread behavior, and `shadcn_flutter` or token-driven equivalents on
66: Flutter. Do not reproduce a reference as one monolithic component or a pile of inline
67: styles.
68: 
69: This project is strict Flat 2.0: **no visible lines or borders anywhere; adjacent regions are
70: distinguished only through background-color changes.** Remove border/shadow defaults from
71: component libraries before judging fidelity.
72: 
73: ## 4. Preserve real architecture while matching the design
74: 
75: Visual fidelity does not authorize fake data paths:
76: 
77: - React visual components import feature hooks, not stores/transports.
78: - Prometheus Entity Management 3.x owns durable/reactive entities and mutations.
79: - Zustand owns transient interaction state only.
80: - Web persistence uses PGlite; Tauri persistence uses pglite-oxide through Rust commands;
81:   Flutter uses the platform repository behind Rust FFI.
82: - Assistant UI renders the real conversation runtime and shared ContentBlock stream.
83: - Local inference is the first/default working lane; cloud BYOK is optional.
84: 
85: The executable prototype may contain demo state, but production components must bind the
86: same states to real entities and runtime events.
87: 
88: ## 5. Screenshot-driven convergence loop
89: 
90: For each matrix row:
91: 
92: 1. launch the real surface;
93: 2. navigate to the exact state;
94: 3. capture at the refere
